# composio-client

Composio API client for TypeScript, generated from the [v3.1 OpenAPI spec](https://staging-backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/openapi.json) with [hey-api](https://heyapi.dev).

This repo is the successor to the Stainless-generated [`@composio/client`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@composio/client) (Stainless is sunsetting). Current scope: the full `/api/v3.1` surface — all 104 released operations — in **both** languages: TypeScript at the package root, and Python in [`python/`](./python/README.md) (PyPI takeover pending). Migration is tracked on the wayfinder map [UXE-152](https://linear.app/composio/issue/UXE-152).

## Usage

The package root is the Stainless-compatible drop-in surface: `new Composio({ apiKey })`, the Stainless type names, and throwing `APIPromise` semantics (shipped via UXE-163/UXE-164).

```ts
import Composio from '@composio/client'

const composio = new Composio({ apiKey: process.env.COMPOSIO_API_KEY })

const session = await composio.toolRouter.session.create({ user_id: 'user_123' })
console.log(session.session_id, session.mcp.url)
```

### Pagination

Use the `@composio/client/pagination` subpath to traverse list operations that return the standard
`items` and `next_cursor` fields:

```ts
import { paginate } from '@composio/client/pagination'

const toolkits = paginate(({ cursor }) =>
  composio.toolkits.list({ cursor, limit: 100 }),
)

for await (const toolkit of toolkits) {
  console.log(toolkit.slug)
}
```

Item iteration is lazy. Each traversal starts from the first page, and breaking early stops fetching
more pages. Use `iterPages()` when page metadata matters, or `toArray()` to collect every item; avoid
`toArray()` when the full result may not fit comfortably in memory.

```ts
for await (const page of toolkits.iterPages()) {
  console.log(page.items.length)
}

const allToolkits = await toolkits.toArray()
```

For another response shape, provide an adapter. Custom cursors must be strings or numbers so repeated
values can be detected reliably across independently decoded pages:

```ts
const results = paginate(
  ({ cursor }) => loadPage(cursor),
  {
    items: page => page.data,
    nextCursor: page => page.nextCursor,
  },
)
```

A repeated cursor cycle throws `ComposioError` instead of requesting pages indefinitely. An empty
cursor ends traversal. When a response omits `next_cursor` but numeric `current_page` and
`total_pages` metadata shows that more pages exist, the default adapter fails instead of silently
returning partial results; provide a custom adapter for that response shape. Requests are sequential
and inherit the normal client retry/backoff path, but this is not proactive/shared rate-limit pacing.

Use `fromEnv` when configuration must come from a specific environment snapshot instead of the
host process. Explicit options replace mapped values, so this is safe for tests, workers, and
applications that load configuration themselves:

```ts
const composio = Composio.fromEnv(config, { environment: 'staging' })
```

`fromEnv` recognizes `COMPOSIO_API_KEY`, `COMPOSIO_USER_API_KEY`, `COMPOSIO_ORG_API_KEY`,
`COMPOSIO_BASE_URL`, `COMPOSIO_ALLOW_INSECURE_HTTP`, `COMPOSIO_CUSTOM_HEADERS`, and
`COMPOSIO_LOG_LEVEL`. Derived clients created with `withOptions()` keep using the resolved snapshot and do
not fall back to ambient values.

Inject a `Transport` when an application or test needs to own HTTP dispatch. The transport receives
a complete `Request`; retries, credential-safe redirects, timeouts, and response parsing stay in the
client:

```ts
import Composio, { createFetchTransport } from '@composio/client'

const transport = createFetchTransport({ fetch: instrumentedFetch })
const composio = new Composio({ apiKey, transport })
```

Existing `fetch` and `fetchOptions` constructor options remain supported. They cannot be combined
with `transport` because a request can have only one HTTP dispatcher.

## Upgrade from Stainless 0.1.x to 2.0

By default, the 2.0 client refuses to send credentials over plain HTTP unless the hostname is
loopback. For a trusted development backend such as Docker's host gateway, opt in to the exact
configured origin:

```ts
const composio = new Composio({
  apiKey,
  baseURL: 'http://host.docker.internal:9900',
  allowInsecureHTTP: true,
})
```

The equivalent environment configuration is:

```sh
COMPOSIO_BASE_URL=http://host.docker.internal:9900 \
COMPOSIO_ALLOW_INSECURE_HTTP=1
```

The opt-in records the resolved scheme, hostname, and port. Mutating `baseURL` cannot broaden it,
and `withOptions({ baseURL: ... })` requires `allowInsecureHTTP: true` again when the origin
changes. Redirects to another origin remain credential-free.

## Development

Toolchain is pinned via [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev) (`mise install`): Node 24, pnpm 11, Python 3.13, uv. ESM-only, TypeScript 7 (native compiler for typechecking, `typescript@6` retained for tooling until 7.1 restores the compiler API).

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm generate       # hey-api + compat codegen: spec/openapi.json → src/generated + src/compat/resources (do not edit)
pnpm lint           # eslint over src, test, codegen, parity, and demo
pnpm typecheck      # tsgo (TS native), including type tests and demo
pnpm typecheck:tsc  # same programs under tsc — both compilers must pass
pnpm codegen:check  # verify committed src/compat/resources matches the generator
pnpm test           # unit tests (MSW mocks) + codegen tests
pnpm build          # tsdown → dist/ (runs publint + arethetypeswrong)
pnpm test:pack      # pack the real tarball, typecheck + import every drop-in subpath
pnpm benchmark:baseline # capture the dist/ a benchmark run compares against
pnpm benchmark      # score SDK overhead against that baseline and against Stainless
pnpm test:contract  # live API tests; requires COMPOSIO_API_KEY (copy .env.example to .env)
pnpm refresh-spec   # re-fetch spec/openapi.json from the live backend
```

`src/generated/` and `src/compat/resources/` are regenerated output — never edit them by hand; CI fails if they drift from `spec/openapi.json`.

### Python lane

The Python client lives in the [`python/`](./python/README.md) workspace (uv-managed):

```sh
pnpm generate:python   # from the repo root: spec snapshot → python/src/composio_client/_generated
cd python
uv sync
uv run ruff check
uv run mypy src scripts
uv run pytest
```

Client-overhead measurements use a deterministic in-memory transport and are documented in
[`docs/benchmarks/client-overhead.md`](./docs/benchmarks/client-overhead.md). They do not measure API
latency.
